text:
Nico Hischier hit 500 career points on Nov. 8 in Toronto, a nice round number for a captain who has spent his whole career, 630 games now, in New Jersey. The season around it is going well too: nine goals in 21 games, seven power-play points, and a Devils team that has won eight of its last ten.

The more interesting number is what happens when he's on the ice at five on five. The Devils get almost 60% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him out there, and he's 4.4 points better than his teammates. Yet his line has scored 4.2 fewer goals than those chances deserve. That's the gap between 14 points and something closer to what his play earns.

His own shooting has run hot, 19% against a likely range around 14%, so the goals may slow while the assists catch up. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 96th percentile for driving offense last season, against top competition. Watch him behind the net: 20% of his setups come from there in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, more than double a typical forward.
